name: Feeling Nature: Which Street View Feels More Positive? (8 Cities)
description:
Method replication: participants choose a city they have lived in for at least one year (Amsterdam, Barcelona, Buenos Aires, Dubai, Nairobi, Quebec City, Singapore or Trondheim), compare 6 pairs of street views from that city and click the one that evokes more positive feelings, then say which elements or aspects made them feel that way and give age and gender. The images are not the paper's stimuli (14–16 Google Street View views per city fetched for this template, 90° field of view at cardinal directions, car roof cropped, 2019–2026 captures).

Original study: Lefosse, Duarte, Sanatani, Kang, van Timmeren & Ratti (2025), "Feeling Nature: Measuring perceptions of biophilia across global biomes using visual AI", npj Urban Sustainability 5, 4. In the online Feeling Nature survey, 400 residents (at least 50 per city, eight cities in different biomes) compared six pairs of street views each and commented on what evoked positive feelings; the pairs came from the top and bottom 5% of Google Street View images scored lively and beautiful by a Place Pulse model, and the answers weighted 25 biophilic classes from semantic segmentation.

Differences from the original study: (1) the images are drawn at random within each city, not from the model's top and bottom lively and beautiful subsets; (2) one comment question at the end instead of feedback with every pair; (3) the segmentation and biophilia metrics are not part of the template.
author: Lefosse, Duarte, Sanatani, Kang, van Timmeren & Ratti
